candidates.name: Intraductal papillary neoplasm of the bile duct
support_spans: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiography demonstrated obstruction of the right hepatic bile duct, compression of the left hepatic duct, and dilation of peripheral bile ducts.
Biliary cytology revealed papillary adenocarcinoma in situ or papillary adenoma with severe atypia.
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and test results, including the obstruction of the right hepatic bile duct and the presence of papillary adenocarcinoma in situ, are consistent with this diagnosis.

candidates.name: Mucinous cystic neoplasm of the liver
support_spans: Abdominal ultrasonography showed a 10 × 15 cm multilocular oval mass with papillary infoldings in the right hepatic lobe.
The cystic lesion was suspected to be a mucin-producing biliary tumor, such as a mucinous cystic neoplasm of the liver or an intraductal papillary neoplasm of the bile duct.
candidates.why: The patient's imaging results, including the multilocular oval mass with papillary infoldings, are consistent with this diagnosis.

candidates.name: Papillary adenocarcinoma
support_spans: Biliary cytology revealed papillary adenocarcinoma in situ or papillary adenoma with severe atypia.
FDG-PET/CT showed intense uptake in the lesion.
candidates.why: The patient's cytology results and imaging findings, including the intense uptake on FDG-PET/CT, are consistent with this diagnosis.
